basis.governing_question: How does Farmácias Lusas choose an ERP, migrate its data and run it in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

sub_questions.question: What must the new ERP do for finance, purchasing and inventory, and where do the current systems fall short?
Which ERP vendor fits the requirements best, and what does the business case show?
How is the chosen ERP configured and tested for finance, purchasing and inventory?
How does data move from the current systems into the ERP and get checked before go-live?
How is the ERP brought live, wave by wave, in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

work.unit: Process area mapped with its requirements

phase_work.why: Three process areas mapped two at a time, plus one week of start-up and one of synthesis; inside the typical 3-6 weeks.
One shortlist, demonstration and scoring round plus a one-week synthesis for the selection gate; inside the typical 4-8 weeks. No formal tender included.

work.unit: System configured and tested for one process area
Rollout wave of up to 10 sites

phase_work.why: Three areas configured two at a time, then migration rehearsal, pilot site, and 41 further sites in five waves of up to 10.

sizing.levers: Running two rollout waves side by side would shorten the engagement most, then configuring all three process areas at once.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Define what finance, purchasing and inventory need from an ERP and where the current systems fall short.

gate.label: Go/no-go on selection
gate.decision: Go or no-go on vendor selection against the agreed requirements and fit-gap?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Compare ERP vendors against the agreed requirements and prepare the selection decision with its business case.

gate.label: Vendor selection
gate.decision: Which ERP vendor does the steering group take forward into implementation?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Configure the ERP, migrate data and roll it out so finance, purchasing and inventory run in all pharmacies and warehouses.

gate.label: Final acceptance
gate.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

architect_notes: Engagement length is an estimate: Implementation takes the middle of its range, and longer configuration cycles or rollout waves push it to the top.
Implementation is added to the archetype's Diagnostic and Design phases because the brief asks for migration and rollout, sized from the archetype's units.
Rollout assumes one pilot site, then the other 41 sites, warehouses included, in five waves of up to 10, run one at a time.
Design excludes a formal tender (4-6 weeks more); confirm whether the client must run one or the contract is large.
No Change & Training phase: the brief names none; confirm whether pharmacy staff training needs its own phase beyond the rollout waves.
